# onetsolutions_instance (Resource)

Manages an OnetSolutions compute instance, a billed order on its billing cycle.

~> **Billing.** Creating this resource **places an order**: the instance is billed on its
`billing_cycle` (monthly or longer) from the moment it is created, with the add-ons of
`addon_ids`. A resize is an upgrade order too, applied once paid. `terraform plan` shows the price
of each order as a warning.

!> **Destroying cancels at the end of the billing period.** Neither `terraform destroy` nor a
change that replaces the instance (`image_id`) deletes it: both request its cancellation at the
end of the current billing period, with `cancellation_reason_code` and `cancellation_reason`. The
instance **keeps running and is billed until `billing_end_date`**, then it is terminated with its
data. The resource leaves the state at once, with a warning giving that date, so a replacement
bills the old instance and the new one side by side until then. To keep the instance, revoke the
cancellation in the console before that date and import it again. `deletion_protection = true`
refuses the destroy.

## Changes

`name`, `tags`, `vpc_id` and `state` change in place; on a new instance, `tags` and `vpc_id` are
applied once it is installed. `size_id` changes in place through a resize order, with
`billing_cycle` if it changes too (the cycle can only change with a new size, to a longer cycle).
A resize needs the instance stopped: it is refused on a running instance unless
`allow_stopping_for_update` is true. Only `image_id` replaces the instance.

`ipv6_enabled = true` gives the instance a public IPv6 address (`primary_ipv6`), at no cost: on a
new instance once it is installed, otherwise in place. The operating system picks the address up at
its next reboot. IPv6 cannot be disabled: `false` on an instance that has it, including one enabled
in the console, is refused at plan time; leave the attribute unset to follow the instance.

## Create-only inputs

These inputs are applied when the instance is installed. Changing one after creation **does not
replace** the instance (that would destroy a billed server and its data): the new value is stored
in the state with a plan-time warning, and takes effect only when the instance is reinstalled or
replaced; that holds for an input left unset at creation and set later too. After an import they
are taken from the configuration without a warning, until the next apply.

| Input | What it sets at installation |
|---|---|
| `ssh_key_ids` | The SSH keys installed for the administrator account |
| `volume_id` | The volume configuration of the size, instead of its default (imported instances only) |
| `control_panel` | A control panel installed after creation |
| `one_click_app` | One Click Apps installed with the instance |
| `addon_ids` | Paid add-ons ordered with the instance |
| `accepted_contract_ids` | The contract versions accepted with the order |
| `install_management_key` | Whether the OnetSolutions support SSH key is installed |
| `allow_password_reset` | Whether the console may change the system password later |

## Cancellation requested outside Terraform

An instance cancelled in the console stays in the state: the refresh fills
`cancellation_requested_at` and `billing_end_date`, warns that the instance ends on that date, and
plans nothing (no replacement, no change). Revoking the cancellation clears both attributes on the
next refresh. Once the instance is terminated (`status` is `terminated` or `cancelled`), it leaves
the state, and the next plan orders a new instance: remove it from the configuration to let it
end, or revoke the cancellation to keep it.

## Unpaid orders

An instance is created once its order is paid. When the account balance does not cover the order,
the apply stops right after ordering with the order number, its **local order id**, the invoice
and the payment link: nothing is added to the state, since no instance exists yet. **Do not apply
the same configuration again before importing it**: that orders a second instance. The plan's
price warning says when the balance does not cover the amount due.

1. Pay the invoice in the console (or through the payment link of the error).
2. Once the instance is created, import it by its order:

   ```shell
   terraform import onetsolutions_instance.web order:<local_order_id>
   ```

   or, with an `import` block, `id = "order:<local_order_id>"`. Until the instance exists, the
   import fails with "The order has no instance yet": wait a few minutes and run it again.
3. Run `terraform plan`: with the configuration that placed the order, it plans nothing.

## Timeouts and failures

If the response to an order is lost (timeout, server error), the apply stops without recording
anything in the state: check the console before applying again.

A create that fails or times out after the instance appeared (a slow installation) keeps the
instance in the state, marked **tainted**: the next apply would replace it, which cancels it and
orders a new one. To keep it, wait until it is active and run `terraform untaint` on its address.
A resize that fails or times out (its invoice unpaid) starts the instance again when it was
stopped for the resize; the size changes once the invoice is paid.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onetsolutions_instance_size" "small" {
  slug = "p-4"
}

data "onetsolutions_image" "debian" {
  os_name    = "Debian"
  os_version = "13"
  visibility = "public"
}

resource "onetsolutions_ssh_key" "admin" {
  name       = "admin"
  public_key = file("~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub")
}

resource "onetsolutions_vpc" "private" {
  name       = "private"
  cidr_block = "10.0.0.0/16"
}

# Creating this resource places an order billed on billing_cycle. Destroying it requests its
# cancellation at the end of the billing period: it keeps running, and billed, until then.
resource "onetsolutions_instance" "web" {
  name          = "web-1"
  size_id       = data.onetsolutions_instance_size.small.id
  image_id      = data.onetsolutions_image.debian.id
  billing_cycle = "monthly"
  vpc_id        = onetsolutions_vpc.private.id
  tags          = ["web", "production"]

  # Public IPv6, at no cost. Once enabled it cannot be disabled.
  ipv6_enabled = true

  # Applied at installation only.
  ssh_key_ids = [onetsolutions_ssh_key.admin.id]

  # Let the provider stop and restart the instance when size_id changes.
  allow_stopping_for_update = true
  deletion_protection       = true

  # Sent with the cancellation once deletion_protection is lifted and the resource destroyed.
  cancellation_reason_code = "no_longer_needed"
  cancellation_reason      = "This server is replaced by a larger one next month."

  timeouts {
    create = "45m"
  }
}

output "web_ipv4" {
  value = onetsolutions_instance.web.primary_ipv4
}

output "web_ipv6" {
  value = onetsolutions_instance.web.primary_ipv6
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `image_id` (String) The UUID of the image to install (see `onetsolutions_image`). Changing it replaces the instance.
- `name` (String) The hostname of the instance, such as `web-1` or `web-1.example.com`. Can be changed in place.
- `size_id` (String) The UUID of the size (see `onetsolutions_instance_size`). Can be changed in place to a size the instance is eligible to (checked at plan time): the resize is an upgrade order, applied once paid, and needs the instance stopped, so it is refused unless `allow_stopping_for_update` is true.

### Optional

- `accepted_contract_ids` (Set of String) The UUIDs of the contract versions accepted with the order. Applied when the instance is installed only: a later change is stored in the state with a plan-time warning and takes effect only on a reinstall or a new instance; it never replaces the instance.
- `addon_ids` (Set of String) Paid add-ons ordered with the instance, at most 20: an add-on id or slug of the chosen size. They are billed on the same order. Applied when the instance is installed only: a later change is stored in the state with a plan-time warning and takes effect only on a reinstall or a new instance; it never replaces the instance.
- `allow_password_reset` (Boolean) Whether the console may change the operating system's password later. Defaults to `true`. Applied when the instance is installed only: a later change is stored in the state with a plan-time warning and takes effect only on a reinstall or a new instance; it never replaces the instance.
- `allow_stopping_for_update` (Boolean) Whether the provider may stop a running instance to change its size, then start it again. Defaults to `false`: a new `size_id` on a running instance is refused at plan time.
- `billing_cycle` (String) The billing cycle, one of `hourly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `semi_annually`, `annually`, `biennially`, `triennially`. Defaults to `monthly`. `hourly` exists only on instances already billed hourly, such as imported ones: a new instance cannot be ordered hourly. The cycle changes only together with a new `size_id`, and only to a longer cycle.
- `cancellation_reason` (String) A sentence of at least 7 words explaining the cancellation, sent with `cancellation_reason_code` when the resource is destroyed or replaced. When unset, a default sentence is recorded. Sent only by the destroy: a change is stored without any request.
- `cancellation_reason_code` (String) Why the instance is cancelled when the resource is destroyed or replaced, one of `too_expensive`, `no_longer_needed`, `missing_feature`, `technical_issue`, `switching_provider`, `other`. Defaults to `no_longer_needed`. Sent only by the destroy: a change is stored without any request, so set it and apply before destroying.
- `control_panel` (String) The slug or UUID of a control panel to install after creation (see `onetsolutions_control_panels`). Applied when the instance is installed only: a later change is stored in the state with a plan-time warning and takes effect only on a reinstall or a new instance; it never replaces the instance.
- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Whether destroying (or replacing) the instance is refused. Defaults to `false`. Set it to `false` and apply before destroying a protected instance.
- `install_management_key` (Boolean) Whether the OnetSolutions support SSH key is installed. Support and the console's tools (such as password reset) need it. Defaults to `true`. Applied when the instance is installed only: a later change is stored in the state with a plan-time warning and takes effect only on a reinstall or a new instance; it never replaces the instance.
- `ipv6_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the instance has public IPv6, at no cost. `true` enables it (on a new instance, once installed); the operating system picks the address up at its next reboot. IPv6 cannot be disabled: `false` on an instance that has it is refused at plan time. When unset, it follows the instance.
- `one_click_app` (Block List) A One Click App installed with the instance; repeat the block for several. Applied when the instance is installed only: a later change is stored in the state with a plan-time warning and takes effect only on a reinstall or a new instance; it never replaces the instance. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--one_click_app))
- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `ssh_key_ids` (Set of String) The UUIDs of the SSH keys (see `onetsolutions_ssh_key`) installed for the administrator account. Applied when the instance is installed only: a later change is stored in the state with a plan-time warning and takes effect only on a reinstall or a new instance; it never replaces the instance.
- `state` (String) The power state, `running` or `stopped`. Defaults to `running`. A new instance with `stopped` is stopped once installed. A change starts or stops the instance.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags, at most 20, unique ignoring case: 1 to 50 letters, digits, spaces, dots, hyphens and underscores, starting with a letter or a digit and not ending with a space. Can be changed in place. On a new instance, they are set once the instance is installed.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `volume_id` (String) The UUID of the volume configuration of the size the instance is installed on, instead of the size's default. Only for imported instances; cannot be set on a new instance. Applied when the instance is installed only: a later change is stored in the state with a plan-time warning and takes effect only on a reinstall or a new instance; it never replaces the instance.
- `vpc_id` (String) The UUID of the VPC (see `onetsolutions_vpc`) the instance joins. Can be changed or removed in place. On a new instance, the VPC is attached once the instance is installed.

### Read-Only

- `billing_end_date` (String) The day a requested cancellation takes effect (RFC 3339): the instance runs and is billed until then. Null when no cancellation is requested.
- `cancellation_requested_at` (String) When a cancellation at the end of the billing period was requested (RFC 3339), null when none is. Set by a destroy, or by a cancellation requested in the console: the instance then stays in the state, unchanged, until it is terminated.
- `created` (String) When the instance was created (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) The UUID of the instance.
- `ip_addresses` (Attributes List) Every IP address of the instance. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ip_addresses))
- `is_installed` (Boolean) Whether the operating system is installed.
- `locked` (Boolean) Whether an operation in progress (backup, snapshot, restore…) locks the instance.
- `next_billing_date` (String) The next renewal date (RFC 3339), null when none is scheduled.
- `order_id` (String) The UUID of the order the instance was created from (the order's local id), null for older instances.
- `os_name` (String) The name of the installed operating system.
- `primary_ipv4` (String) The primary public IPv4 address.
- `primary_ipv6` (String) The primary public IPv6 address, null when IPv6 is not enabled.
- `recurring_amount` (String) The amount billed at each renewal, excluding tax, as a decimal string.
- `status` (String) The status of the service: `pending`, `provisioning`, `active`, `suspended`, `terminated`, `cancelled` or `error`.
- `volumes` (Attributes List) The volumes of the instance. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--volumes))

- `delete` (String) How long to wait for the deletion, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `5m`.
- `update` (String) How long to wait for the update, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `30m`.

- `is_primary` (Boolean) Whether it is the primary address of its family.

- `name` (String) The name of the volume.
- `size_gb` (Number) The size of the volume in GB.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# For an instance whose invoice was paid after the apply stopped, the id is
# "order:<local_order_id>".
import {
  to = onetsolutions_instance.web
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9b8a7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-8c2d-1e0f9a8b7c6d"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<id>, or <id> when the provider sets organization_id and project_id.
# The create-only inputs (ssh_key_ids, volume_id, control_panel, one_click_app, addon_ids,
# accepted_contract_ids) are taken from the configuration after an import, without a warning.
terraform import onetsolutions_instance.web 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9b8a7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-8c2d-1e0f9a8b7c6d

# An instance whose order was waiting for payment is imported by that order once the invoice is
# paid: order:<local_order_id>, optionally after <organization_id>/<project_id>/.
terraform import onetsolutions_instance.web order:5d4c3b2a-1f0e-4d9c-8b7a-6f5e4d3c2b1a
```
